title: Hopper FP8 profile: calibration pipeline, INT8 fallback, and stability hardening
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Deliver a hardened FP8 serving profile for Hopper GPUs that includes a reproducible calibration pipeline, safety nets (INT8/FP32 fallback), and fixes for observed numeric instability. This ticket covers: (1) per-model calibration harness for automated E4M3 vs E5M2 selector, (2) runtime checks for overflow/underflow and automatic re-quantization, (3) telemetry and regression gates for accuracy/perplexity, and (4) operational rollout strategy with canaries and automatic fallbacks. Background: internal experiments showed mixed accuracy across decoder and encoder-decoder families when using naive FP8 scales on Hopper kernels. Several instability modes were identified during initial enablement runs (scale blowup on KV cache, subtle nondeterminism in fused kernels, and rare nan/inf during long generation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Calibration harness produces stable per-layer scales for 95% of models in the internal catalog using the standard calibration corpus.
- E4M3/E5M2 selector achieves <=0.5% perplexity regression vs baseline FP32 across validation set for selected models, otherwise defaults to INT8/FP32.
- Runtime detects overflow cases in <5ms and triggers safe re-quantization or fallback with no user-visible request failure.
- Telemetry captures per-request scale stats, overflow events, and selected profile; dashboards updated.
- End-to-end smoketest and perf bench added to CI gating for the release branch.
work_log: 2025-01-28: Kickoff — scoped calibration corpus (1M tokens, mixed open-domain + instruction), set initial success thresholds.
2025-01-31: Reproduced NaN propagation on long-generation tests; root cause traced to KV-cache quantize/dequantize asymmetry when using per-layer dynamic scales.
2025-02-03: Prototype fix — clamp dynamic scales at layer-level using a percentile-based bound; reduced NaN rate to near-zero in unit runs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/998
2025-02-07: Built automated calibration job that produces candidate profiles and runs validation harness; discovered encoder-decoders prefer E5M2 in several cases.
2025-02-11: Added runtime overflow detector and re-quantization path; instrumented telemetry event keys for scale and overflow counts (dashboard pending).
2025-02-15: Integration tests failing intermittently on kernels with async streams — investigating kernel launch ordering and stream synchronization.
Next steps: stabilize stream sync, expand calibration to additional model families, add canary rollout plan in Console.
decisions: Default profile selector: run calibration offline to propose E4M3 or E5M2; if proposed profile exceeds accuracy threshold, accept, otherwise fallback to INT8/FP32.
Clamp strategy: compute layer scale percentiles (99.5th) during calibration and apply a global per-layer clamp to prevent runaway scales at runtime.
Runtime safety: on overflow or >3 scale adjustments in a single request, automatically re-run the request using INT8 if available, else FP32.
Telemetry retention: keep per-profile aggregates for 90 days, per-request sample logs for 7 days for debugging.
Canary policy: start with 5% traffic to FP8 for models that pass calibration, increase to 25% after 48 hours with no regressions.
testing_plan: Calibration: run automated calibration harness on catalog subset (gpt-small/coder-like/t5-medium families) and store scale tables in S3.
Accuracy validation: compute perplexity, token-level logprob delta, and downstream task metrics (exact match/ROUGE where applicable); threshold: <=0.5% perplexity increase or <=1% task metric drop.
Stress: long-generation workloads (>=2048 tokens) run for 10k requests to catch rare numeric issues; assert <0.01% request-level failure rate.
A/B Perf: measure p50/p95 latency delta and token/sec for E4M3 vs E5M2 vs INT8 on Hopper; target: no more than 10% p50 latency increase for safety paths.
CI: add nightly job that runs calibration + validation on a representative model matrix and fails the release candidate on regressions.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge runtime PR with calibration harness and overflow detector behind a feature flag.
2) Run full-catalog offline calibration and populate profile store with candidates and confidence scores.
3) Enable FP8 canary for internal orgs only (5% traffic) for models that pass validation.
4) Monitor telemetry dashboard for 48-72 hours, check accuracy/perf/overflow metrics, roll forward to 25% then 100% incrementally.
5) If at any stage overflow or accuracy regression exceeds thresholds, automatically revert to previous profile and create incident link.
notes: Avoid coupling selector to hardware SKU; selector should be model-and-workload-driven. We should also coordinate with Dedicated team to expose profile telemetry for reserved pools. Follow up task: add explicit test harness for multi-GPU stream ordering to catch the async kernel sync intermittency.
